title: Statistics - Lesson 6: Interpreting Box Plots Practice
description: Practice reading and interpreting medians, IQRs, ranges, whiskers, and context from box plots.

questions.question: In a box plot, which feature shows the median?
options: The full length from minimum to maximum
questions.explanation: The median is represented by the line drawn inside the box.

questions.question: A box plot has Q1 = 18 and Q3 = 31. What is the IQR? Enter just the number.
Class A has median score 84. Class B has median score 79. Which statement is supported?
options: Class B has the higher typical score.
Class A has the higher typical score.
Class A must have the smaller range.
Class B must have no outliers.
questions.explanation: The higher median indicates the higher typical value, so Class A has the higher typical score.

questions.question: A wider box means the middle 50% of data values are more spread out.
questions.explanation: The box width represents the interquartile range, which measures spread in the middle 50% of the data.

questions.question: Group X has IQR 8. Group Y has IQR 20. Which group is more consistent in the middle 50%?
options: There is not enough information to compare medians
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR means the middle half of the data is less spread out, so Group X is more consistent.

questions.question: A box plot has minimum 12 and maximum 47. What is the range? Enter just the number.
A box plot has a much longer right whisker than left whisker. What does this suggest?
options: The data must have a larger sample size.
The median is equal to the maximum.
questions.explanation: A longer right whisker suggests that higher values are more spread out, which is a right-skew clue.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain why using only the maximum value can lead to a weak comparison of two box plots.
questions.correctAnswer: The maximum may be only one value and may not represent the typical data. A stronger comparison also uses the median, IQR, and range in context.
questions.explanation: A complete comparison should not rely on a single extreme value; it should consider center and spread.
